title: Operator‑led access request scoring & triage playbook
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Objective: Define a concise, operator-friendly playbook and automated intake pipeline for non-bug admin & access requests (RBAC changes, SSO/SAML onboarding, SCIM provisioning, org policy exceptions). The playbook's goal is to reduce mean time to resolution, standardize risk handling, and ensure high-touch enterprise customers receive predictable SLAs while keeping engineering involvement minimal.
description_long:
Scope: inbound requests from CSMs, Support, Security, and self-serve forms. Excludes incident/SEV response (handled by SRE) and ad-hoc engineering feature work. Key outcomes: 1) a deterministic scoring rubric to prioritize requests; 2) automated routing to Admin Ops vs Engineering vs Security/Compliance queues; 3) templated runbooks and acceptance criteria to enable canary/batch work; 4) telemetry to monitor throughput, SLA adherence, and regression signals.

Scoring heuristic (proposed):
- Customer tier weight (Enterprise=5, Midmarket=3, Startup=1)
- Data sensitivity modifier (PHI/PII/Regulated=+4, Internal-only=0)
- Risk of privilege scope (Org-wide admin=+5, Team-level role=+2)
- Automation readiness (SCIM-ready=false -> +3 manual effort)
- Compliance/regulatory trigger (requires audit/logging=+4)
- Time-sensitivity multiplier (legal/SLA breach=2x)
Final score -> route: 0–4 = self-serve / docs; 5–8 = Admin Ops (SLA 5 business days); 9–12 = Escalate to Engineering+Security (SLA 3 business days); 13+ = Exec review + legal loop (SLA 48 hours for acknowledgement).

Channels & integrations: Confluence intake template + Google Form for structured fields; Zendesk ticket tag mapping and webhook to Linear; auto-create Linear issue with labels and populated metadata; Slack #admin-triage channel for high-score alerts.

Acceptance criteria for routing to Engineering: clear reproducible steps, minimal manual steps for Admin Ops, design doc or PR template if code changes required, defined rollback path.

Trade-offs discussed: We prefer operator-first automation to reduce eng load but accept some false positives early to avoid missed high-risk requests. Full automation of RBAC diffs is deferred until ENG tasks in release runtime-1.18 are delivered.
